transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-12-03 14:00 PST | Duration 75m
Attendees: Ava Chen, Marco Reyes, Priya Patel, Samir Gupta, Lena Ortiz, Diego Morales, Hannah Kim, Chris Wang, Olivia Park

Summary: Quick sync to align Q1 roadmap items with launch readiness for the Dedicated offering, review the recent KV cache incident, and confirm release gating and observability items.
Topics: roadmap alignment, launch checklist, incident follow-up, rollout windows, security signoffs.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Ava Chen: okay let's get started, thanks everyone for joining, uh we wanted to keep this tight 75 minutes, roadmap and launch readiness for Dedicated primarily, and a quick incident review. Olivia you're on for release checklist right?
[00:18] Olivia Park: yep, I have the checklist deck, i'll share after the call, slide deck link: https://redwood.app/s/roadmap-q1-launch (shared). it's in draft, needs SOC2 items confirmed.
[00:32] Marco Reyes: cool. i'll start with infra: we've nailed down the autoscale policies for Dedicated pools, main risk left is the burst capacity gating with the lane that crosses hosted, there's a throttle case we haven't stress tested.
[00:48] Priya Patel: speaking of stress tests, i kicked off a series last night simulating steady state 120k tokens/min and bursts to 400k for 10 minutes. saw increased tail p99 on seq len 2k, suspect KV cache thrash.
[01:05] Samir Gupta: yeah that matches the incident last week — the KV cache eviction storm, um logs showed rapid cache churn when multiple models hit warm-up sequences. we pushed a fix to reduce eviction aggressiveness but need integration tests.
[01:22] Hannah Kim: quick security note, we need the KMS audit logs present and immutable for the release, and SSO/SAML signoff, plus the privacy team wants a data retention policy. i sent a checklist in the security channel.
[01:40] Ava Chen: great, so can we align on owners: Olivia handles release checklist and gating, Priya does the autoscale tests and validation, Samir gets the KV cache patch and integration tests, Marco surfaces rollout windows, and Lena runs regression tests.
[01:57] Lena Ortiz: yep i'll pick up regression and qps cap tests, want to ensure no perf regressions with the quantized variants we plan to ship.
[02:12] Diego Morales: also want to call out operational runbooks — the incident response playbook for KV cache needs clearer steps; right now it's a bit scattered between infra runbooks and the runtime team notes.
[02:28] Chris Wang: agreed, i'll consolidate runbooks into the ops repo and link in the release checklist. action: consolidate runbooks -> ops repo.

[02:45] (auto-generated topics interjection)
Summary bullets (auto-gen): - KV cache eviction caused brief outage for multi-tenant workloads - Need more robust autoscale stress tests - Security/KMS audit logs required for release - Rollout windows and canary gating to be defined

[03:05] Marco Reyes: for rollout windows, thinking of a 3-phase rollout: canary -> regional gradual -> full, each phase with automated rollback on error rates and latency regression. need to pick peak/off-peak windows for each region.
[03:25] Priya Patel: and establish traffic steering to fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, we've done RFC for smart routing but need testing across regions, esp eu-west.
[03:42] Samir Gupta: small note on model variants: quantized bits 4 vs 8 affect latency and mem pressure; our batcher behavior changes, so regression matrix must include quantization profiles.
[03:58] Ava Chen: good. Hannah, security gating — what's blocking us?
[04:08] Hannah Kim: mainly SOC2 evidence for the Private control plane and KMS integration test results. also RBAC audit and SSO tests. i need Olivia to attach the final CA cert rotation schedule.
[04:24] Olivia Park: i'll add that into the checklist doc, will also attach the compliance spreadsheet.

[04:35] (15 min mark skipped)
[05:10] Priya Patel: on the incident postmortem, quick recap: 2025-11-28 at 03:12 UTC we had a KV cache eviction event that increased RPC latency and caused backpressure, traffic queued up and some timeouts triggered. root cause was cache eviction policy mismatch and a rare sequence length distribution that wasn't covered in benchmarks.
[05:32] Samir Gupta: mitigation we applied was to reduce eviction aggressiveness and increase per-host cache size, but that had memory tradeoffs. long term fix: smarter eviction TTL and prefix-aware caching.
[05:48] Marco Reyes: do we have numbers on customer impact? Diego?
[05:55] Diego Morales: impacted approx 12 customers, spike in errors ~1.2% for 7 minutes, sla not breached but customer tickets rose. it triggered an oncall page and CS outreach.
[06:10] Ava Chen: okay that aligns with incident severity 3. We need a postmortem doc, timeline, RCA, and long term action items. Samir/Priya to own.

[06:25] Lena Ortiz: QA found a regression in the generation path when we toggled a new kernel selection; it's intermittent but correlates with certain prompt patterns — could be tokenization subtlety.
[06:40] Samir Gupta: that might be tied to the kernel selection heuristics; i'll reproduce locally and add tests.

[06:55] (artifact mention)
Priya Patel: test results and the stress test script are in the infra repo, link: https://confluence.redwood/infa/autoscale-tests (typo in transcript may vary).

[07:10] Olivia Park: about docs, release checklist currently has gating: security signoff, perf signoff, regression pass, runbooks consolidated, and postmortem for recent incidents attached. if any of those fail, we revert to no-release.
[07:25] Hannah Kim: on compliance there's one item — data residency for eu customers; we must ensure region pinning and that audit logs are kept in-region or we have a justify doc.
[07:39] Marco Reyes: operationally we can do region pinning, but that increases complexity for smart routing. need to model cost/latency tradeoffs.

[07:54] (Mid call, crosstalk)
[08:10] Ava Chen: let's go through the launch checklist quickly and mark who is blocked. Olivia can you share the doc live?
[08:20] Olivia Park: sharing now, live doc: /docs/releases/q1-dedicated-checklist (link posted). first item: perf signoff.
[08:30] Marco Reyes: perf signoff: Marco/Samir/Priya — status: in progress, target 2025-12-10.
[08:39] Samir Gupta: regression tests in 2 days, full matrix by 2025-12-09.
[08:46] Lena Ortiz: i'll run the regression suite and surface any blockers same day.

[08:55] Priya Patel: autoscaling validation notes: observed p99 latency 450ms under burst before fixes, after patch p99 dropped to 220ms but still spiky on long sequences. will instrument more metrics for model sequence length bucketing.
[09:14] Chris Wang: ops will add sequence length histograms to console dashboards. will need frontend ticket but low effort.
[09:24] Ava Chen: great. other risks?
[09:29] Diego Morales: dependency on external infra team for the canary infra scaffold may delay rollout by a week if not prioritized. we should escalate to platform PM.
[09:40] Marco Reyes: noted, i'll raise in platform sync.

[09:46] (Noise, small interruption)
[10:05] Olivia Park: last bit on communications: CSMs need a launch brief and persona-specific notes, i'll draft and share, CS to review.
[10:17] Diego Morales: i'll coordinate the customer outreach plan and templated messages.

[10:25] Ava Chen: ok to recap next steps: Olivia finalizes checklist, Priya runs autoscale stress tests, Samir lands KV cache patch, Marco drafts rollout windows, Lena completes regression testing, Hannah updates SOC2 items. we'll meet next week same time to validate gating progress.
[10:44] (wrap)
[10:50] Ava Chen: any blockers or questions? (silence) alright thank you all, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: some names/tokens may be misrecognized (e.g., KV cache spelled as K-V cakhe in raw auto transcript), timestamps approximate.

Referenced artifacts: slides https://redwood.app/s/roadmap-q1-launch, infra stress tests https://confluence.redwood/infa/autoscale-tests, release checklist /docs/releases/q1-dedicated-checklist.
